feedback.problem:
Let $c=[\begin{aligned}-2 \\ 0 \\ 1\end{aligned}]$ and $d=[\begin{aligned}2 \\ 3 \\ 4\end{aligned}].$ Find the vector projection of $c$ onto $d.$

${\text{proj}}_{d}\,c=⟨$

{{field-1}},

{{field-2}},

{{field-3}}

$⟩$
feedback.worked_solution:
Using the formula for the vector projection, we obtain

$$
\begin{aligned}{\text{proj}}_{d}\,c & =\frac{c\cdot d}{d\cdot d}d \\  & =\frac{{c}_{x}{d}_{x}+{c}_{y}{d}_{y}+{c}_{z}{d}_{z}}{{d}_{x}^{2}+{d}_{y}^{2}+{d}_{z}^{2}}d \\  & =\frac{(-2)\cdot 2+0\cdot 3+1\cdot 4}{{2}^{2}+{3}^{2}+{4}^{2}}d \\  & =\frac{0}{29}d \\  & =⟨0,0,0⟩.\end{aligned}
$$
